cards.text: This is a song of David, the shepherd who became Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3). No warm-up, no 'hope this finds you well.' He opens by asking the LORD to fight against those who fight against him.

cards.question: David's asking the LORD to step into the fight for him. What does he ask the LORD to take up?

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to draw the spear and javelin against his pursuers. Shield, buckler, spear, javelin, friend, that's not a prayer request, that's a WHOLE ARMORY!

cards.question: Weapons aren't all David asks for. What does he ask the LORD to tell his soul?

answers.text: That the fight is almost over

cards.text: Next, David turns to the people out to get him. He asks that those who seek his life be disgraced and put to shame, driven back and confounded.

cards.question: David asks that his enemies be like chaff in the wind. Who does he picture driving them away?

cards.text: And their road? Dark and slick, with the angel of the LORD pursuing. Picture sprinting across an icy parking lot at night with somebody right behind you, and you've got the idea.

cards.question: David says his enemies laid a net for him and dug a pit for his soul. True or false: he says they had good reason to do it.
David asks for ruin to hit his enemies by surprise. True or false: he asks that the net they hid for him would catch them instead.

cards.text: Then the whole song changes direction. David looks past the fight to the day the LORD saves him.

cards.question: David says that when the LORD saves him, his soul will ___ in the LORD.

cards.text: Then David says all his bones will exclaim, “Who is like You, O LORD…” ALL his bones, friend! Me, the only noise I make is when I bend down to the bottom oven.

cards.question: True or false: in that shout from all his bones, David says the LORD delivers the poor and needy from the robber.

cards.text: Now it gets personal. Hostile witnesses come forward with charges David knows nothing about, like getting a bill for a gym membership you never signed up for.

cards.question: David says these people repay him ___ for ___.

cards.text: And here's what makes it sting. When those same people were ill, David put on sackcloth and humbled himself with fasting.

cards.question: True or false: David says his prayers back then came back answered.
While those people were ill, David was bowed down with grief. Who does he say he grieved like someone mourning for?

cards.text: Then the tables turn. This time David is the one who stumbles.

cards.question: When David stumbled, what did these people do?

cards.text: Even assailants David didn't know slandered him without ceasing. Total strangers piling on, friend, that's a comments section!

cards.question: True or false: David says they gnashed their teeth at him like godless jesters at a feast.

cards.text: Then David turns to the Lord with a question. I bet a lot of hurting people have asked it too.

cards.question: What does David ask the Lord while all this is going on?

answers.text: How long will You look on

cards.text: He asks the Lord to rescue his precious life “from these lions.” And I thought the junk drawer was rough, friend. David's out here dealing with LIONS.

cards.question: Once the Lord rescues him, where does David say he'll give thanks?

cards.text: Now David asks the LORD not to let his enemies gloat over him, people who hate him without reason and wink in malice. The WINK, friend, nothing good has ever come after a wink like that.

cards.question: David says these enemies don't speak peace. Who does he say they devise deceitful schemes against?

answers.text: Those who live quietly in the land
The elders at the city gate

cards.text: They gape at him and say, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen!” That's the neighbor at the window who's been WAITING all week to watch you back into the mailbox.

cards.question: David's enemies brag that their eyes have seen. What does David tell the LORD right back?
David asks the LORD not to be ___ and not to be far from him.

cards.text: Then David cries out, “Awake and rise to my defense, to my cause, my God and my Lord!” That's a man who knows exactly who's got his back.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to vindicate him. What does he ask Him to vindicate him by?

cards.text: He asks the LORD not to let them say, “We have swallowed him up!” Friend, I spent years swallowed up in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, David does NOT want that.

cards.question: True or false: David asks that those who exalt themselves over him be clothed in honor.

cards.text: But not everybody's against David. Some people want to see him vindicated.

cards.question: True or false: David wants the people who favor his vindication to stay quiet and wait.
David wants those people to always say the LORD delights in something. What is it?

cards.text: And just like before, David finishes with praise. His tongue will proclaim the LORD's righteousness and His praises.

cards.question: True or false: David says his tongue will proclaim the LORD's praises all day long.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess which pair of armor words the psalm uses (shield and buckler vs sword and bow). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason to the right pair. This is the same kind of detail guess as the Psalm 23 bad example (oil, myrrh or perfume).

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences: 'And their road?' / 'Dark and slick, with the angel of the LORD pursuing.' / 'Picture sprinting…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Verse 6 is a wish ('May their path be dark and slick'). 'And their road? Dark and slick' tells it as a fact about the enemies' road instead of something David asks for.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences: 'Then David says all his bones will exclaim…' / 'ALL his bones, friend!' / 'Me, the only noise I make…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answers 'evil' and 'good' are moral qualities. The wrong answers 'silver', 'gold' and 'land' are possessions, so they are a different kind of thing, and the right pair stands out right away.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess which relative the psalm names (mother vs son vs king). The earlier cards give nothing to reason from, so this is a wording-detail guess and not a question about the movement or the meaning.
